findings.area: B4-M1 PRE_IO durable safety obligation lifecycle
findings.statement: The proposed PRE_IO obligation is a register-and-protected-settle pair, not a closed lifecycle. (a) No ordinary verified-success disposition exists: b_settle_node_safety_obligation is sv_b_operator-only and requires 'independent authenticated physical cleanup proof + protected clear/restore record'; an obligation registered before an ordinary successful GPU exchange or build dispatch therefore keeps the Node ineligible until an operator settles it, or an unspecified ordinary settle path exists, which would contradict 'cannot become implicit release/clear/success'. (b) The actual IO call sites the obligation must precede are not named and nothing binds the obligation to the IO, so precedence is not checkable. (c) 'Every eligibility query checks unresolved obligation independently of nodes.status' is a blanket label: none of the actual plain eligibility readers are enumerated or mapped to an obligation-aware read, and the actual source swallows quarantine-fence failure. (d) The symbolic model checks obligations globally and only for B, and has no settle transition.

quarantineFailureSwallowed: services/control-plane/src/inv/build_execution.py:414 and :429 LOGGER.exception after node-agent marker and _mark_node_quarantined failures
contract: plan_specs.py quarantine spec 'physical cleanup already occurred outside'

counterexamples: MA2b: released_state -> pre_io_obligation('gpu-delivery-op') with no failure -> cp_eligible == False permanently (no settle transition in model; matrix settle only sv_b_operator).
MA1: an obligation for another tenant/Node/epoch denies THIS Node (cp_eligible False), so fixture quarantine-EXECUTE-loss-still-denied passes without testing scoping.

Source: build_execution.py:419-431 _mark_node_quarantined fails -> logged and swallowed -> status stays 'online' -> dispatch.py:79 / placement.py:239 still select the Node. The contract wants the obligation to keep it denied, but no plain reader is mapped to check it.
requiredFix: Define the obligation key (tenant_id,node_id,epoch,operation_id) and a closed state machine, e.g. PENDING_IO -> {VERIFIED_CLEAN | UNCERTAIN} -> SETTLED_PROTECTED, with typed procedures and principals per edge.

Ordinary success: sv_b_runtime/verifier may settle PENDING_IO -> VERIFIED_CLEAN only in the same transaction as the exact typed receipt/cleanup evidence (e.g. b_append_build_cleanup_evidence, NodeReceiptStore.record) bound to operation_id, and never from UNCERTAIN.
Any exception or unknown outcome moves the obligation to UNCERTAIN (or leaves it PENDING), and only the protected OP settle with physical proof can reduce it.
Name each registration call site and its committed transaction BEFORE node_transport.py:289 and build_execution.py:787.
Bind the obligation_id/hash into the signed permit / dispatch body / receipt so the Node, adapter or receipt verifier refuses IO, or refuses to accept its outcome, without a committed obligation.

Enumerate every plain and B eligibility reader (at least the 13 sites above) and replace each with one fixed read/lock procedure: status AND no unresolved obligation for that tenant/node/epoch AND containment AND B current-chain conditions where B applies.
Define the denial lattice over inv.nodes {online, offline, draining, quarantined} so 'retain stronger denial / never clear draining' is decidable. Actual source overwrites draining with quarantined.

Model scoped obligations and add settle positive/negative and time-advancing fixtures (success settle, failure->UNCERTAIN, RUN cannot settle UNCERTAIN, OP settle without proof refused, wrong-node obligation does not deny other Nodes, EXECUTE loss still denies the plain readers).

findings.statement: unknownEdges are chosen by bare method-name collision with any reached function name, and every one gets disposition BLOCK_THIS_ENTRY_UNTIL_STATIC_RESOLUTION_OR_ACTUAL_TRACE. The result is 5426 BLOCK edges. That is an effective global boilerplate block, which Root forbade ('required known path must have a concrete supported plan, not global B denial'). Every critical entry that has a concrete plan also carries BLOCK edges in its own transitive closure, so the artifacts contradict themselves, and the real residual unknowns are buried. Plans never reference unknownEdges.

findings.area: B4-M2 explicit rank of proposed B tables
findings.statement: RANK_GROUPS ranks all observed source tables but none of the 21 proposed B tables written by B procedures. These include inv.node_role_safety_obligations, lineage_tombstones, gate_acks, releases, delegations, admissions, leases, delivery_challenges, key_possessions, key_deliveries, request_issuance, request_commits, member_cas, storage_bindings and service_bindings. lockOnlyProcedures.canonicalOrder only names coarse 'role/current' and 'nonce/evidence/ledger' stages, so within-stage order and the position of obligations and tombstones relative to inv.nodes and runs are undecided.
findings.requiredFix: Give every new B table an explicit rank and mode in the same RANK list used for plans, plus per-procedure ranked lock lists (e.g. b_raise_node_quarantine: obligations vs inv.nodes vs outbox).

findings.area: B4-L3 signing-service scope for operator purposes
findings.statement: The History and a model comment say the protected signing service refuses ARM of a revoked or unknown descendant. In model.service_sign the operator policy is kind plus shape only. The lineage check lives in the caller's command(). The Node has no tombstone knowledge, so it ARMs the revoked descendant. The CP CAS still refuses, so the impact is availability/HOLD only.
counterexamples: MA3b service_sign(OP,'GATE_CONTROL', ARM body of revoked lineage) -> signed
findings.requiredFix: Either make GATE_CONTROL ARM / RELEASE / DELEGATION scope validation inside the signing service (current lineage, no tombstone, exact approved tuple) with negatives, or correct the claim so the guarantee is CP-CAS-only.

findings.area: B4-L1 tombstone authenticity and Node propagation
findings.statement: b_revoke_approval_lineage is executable by sv_b_operator and sv_b_safety. The signing policy grants LINEAGE_TOMBSTONE to the operator only, so a safety-initiated tombstone cannot be signed. The LINEAGE_TOMBSTONE domain has no consumer: Node knownLineageRevocations is never populated.
findings.requiredFix: State that CP tombstone authenticity is the DB principal plus causal evidence (unsigned) and remove the domain, or define the signer for SAFE-initiated tombstones and a Node-side consumer/ACK. Keep the Node bound as gate invalidation or expiry.

findings.statement: The contract (Root (e) wording) says activation requires the original Node folder confirmation. The actual 72028 activate_contribution (src/saintvision/services/storage.py:94-112) and API (src/saintvision/api/v1/storage.py:184-195) check only the registered owner and not-revoked. No confirmation artifact is read; the docstring states intent only. A plain wrapper requiring confirmation would change current plain behaviour.
findings.requiredFix: Either name the confirmation artifact (signed Node folder observation bound to contribution_id/normalized_path/channel) and record it as an explicit plain behaviour change, or keep plain activation owner-only and place folder confirmation in the B-only b_approve_readonly_contribution_root prerequisite.
